native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: Both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects in the Social discipline (the df1 'discipline' value Social): 82.0% of the 668 original studies (548/668) and 78.4% of the 668 replication studies (524/668) used student subjects — the closest match to the ~82.4% / ~80.9% benchmarks, with absolute deviations of 0.36 and 2.46 percentage points respectively and a combined L1 distance of 2.82 pp (the minimum across all eight groupings tested, including the four replication projects ml1/ml3/rpp/ee and the other two disciplines Cognitive and Economics).
native_result.WorkflowB: Restricted to df1 (df2 has no joinable key — 0/143 exact matches of df2.study against df1.authors.o or df1.title). Computed per-group marginal student-subject shares P(subjects.o='students') and P(subjects.r='students') for the three disciplines, the four replication projects (ml1/ml3/rpp/ee), and the full df1, then ranked by L1 distance to the target pair (82.4, 80.9). Social wins decisively (L1 2.82), with the next-closest grouping being df1 overall (3.54) and the best project-level grouping being rpp (6.60); ml3, ee and Economics are far too student-saturated (90%+/100%) to match. Reported robustness checks: (i) dropping the single row with NaN in subjects.o/subjects.r leaves Social at 82.16/78.56 pp; (ii) excluding rows with non-null aggregated leaves Social at 83.64/74.55 pp — neither overturns the Social identification. Also computed the alternative joint reading P(O students ∧ R students) by discipline (Social 66.17%, Cognitive 61.83%, Economics 94.44%), which does not approach either benchmark and is presented only to rule out that reading.
